Tara (Docs): FYI — I'm opening a small addendum to the q-profiles docs for short sequence lengths. Hit an edge case while writing migration guidance: certain 4-bit profiles cause token-dropping when seq_len < 64 on the LLaMA-derivative we test against. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567 :eyes:
Alex (SDK): link works. Can you paste the minimal SDK snippet change you want? If it's just max_sequence or truncate logic we can keep it a 1-line example for Python and JS.
Tara (Docs): Thanks — thinking of adding this snippet under "Quant profiles -> Known edge cases" and a short migration note. Proposed snippet: ```python
# when switching to 4-bit profile, ensure client truncates to safe length
resp = client.generate(model="llama-4bit-safe", input="...", max_tokens=32, truncate=True)
```
Alex (SDK): OK. For JS: ```js
// SDK: explicit truncate flag for short sequences
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'llama-4bit-safe', input: '...', maxTokens: 32, truncate: true })
```
Chris (Opt): Quick note: add a line recommending prefix caching instead of eager KV cache priming for short sequences — we saw a perf regression when the runtime attempted full KV materialization for very short requests. Something like: "Prefer prefix/KV prefetch heuristics for seq_len < 128 to avoid unnecessary memory pressure."
Tara (Docs): Good call. I'll add a one-sentence heuristic and link to the runtime doc.
Sam (Eng): Can we also add a tiny unit test snippet that simulates seq_len 16/32 cases? I can contribute a test in the serving repo once the doc wording is final.
Tara (Docs): Awesome — would you prefer test code inline or a link to the test in the PR? I'd rather keep docs small and link out.
Sam (Eng): Link out is fine. I'll open a follow-up PR and link it in the doc.
Jen (PM): timeline: we need this live before the next release train on Tuesday. If reviews are quick can we merge by Monday EOD? :calendar:
Alex (SDK): I can review SDK examples today.
Chris (Opt): I'll review the heuristic wording and add a short benchmark note.
Tara (Docs): Great — tagging reviewers in the PR. doc-bot, created PR 4567 and assigned reviewers.
doc-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567 — reviewers: Alex (SDK), Chris (Opt), Sam (Eng). Status: open.
Tara (Docs): Action items: (1) Alex -> finalize JSX/py snippets, (2) Chris -> wording + link to runtime note, (3) Sam -> follow-up test PR and link back, (4) Tara -> merge after approvals and cherry-pick to v-next.
Alex (SDK): Will push updated snippet in 30m. :clock1:
Chris (Opt): I'll drop a short benchmark note and an image-less perf table (numbers only) to keep docs lightweight.
Sam (Eng): I'll queue the test PR and post the link here once created.
Tara (Docs): Thanks all — ping me if any blockers. If we can't get it approved by Monday EOD we'll stage for the next ship with a prominent "Known issue" callout. :shipit:
